submissions.cause: HardwareClockDiscontinuityCount 5->6 at epoch 149 (TimeNanos and FullBiasNanos both step by 2^32 ms). The loader rebases the receiver-clock reference there, a ~194 m clock step that the positive 100 km clock-jump detector misses; the clock continuity factor then dragged GNSS-first epochs 0-210 by 27-89 m (pseudorange residual median 11-53 m vs 1.2-2.1 m at the archived taroz GNSS-stage positions) and left 2-3.8 m in the final output. Solving epochs 0-147 alone gives 0.6 m.
submissions.inventory: only this drive among the 40 test and 40 train drives changes HardwareClockDiscontinuityCount
submissions.truth_free_diagnostic: horizontal distance to the archived taroz result_gnss_imu test output: median 0.16 -> 0.05 m, P95 3.26 -> 0.10 m

submissions.cause: The static leveling window (first 250 gyro samples, 2.25 s) starts while the car moves at 5 m/s and turns. Its gyro mean (0.0097 rad/s; stop-block mean 0.0004 rad/s) became the initial gyro bias, which the 0.01 rad/s prior and the 5e-7 bias random walk kept (optimized -0.0093 rad/s about the vertical body axis). Body yaw minus GNSS course then rotated at 0.5 deg/s, and the IMU stage left the GNSS-first stage by 2-3 m in curves.
submissions.rule: apply the existing zero-bias initialization only where the leveling-window gyro mean differs from the stop-block gyro mean by more than 0.005 rad/s; among the 40 test drives that is sjc-ce1 alone (0.0100 rad/s; next 0.0031 rad/s)
submissions.train_evidence_note: (P50+P95)/2 without/with --native-source-imu-initialization on the 14 scored static-leveling train drives; the other 12 change by at most 0.001 m. mtv-b Pixel4 (0.0053 rad/s) is the only train drive above the rule; Pixel4XL (0.0007 rad/s) shows why the option is not applied everywhere
submissions.truth_free_diagnostic: horizontal distance to the archived taroz result_gnss_imu test output: median 0.76 -> 0.13 m, P95 2.76 -> 0.33 m

submissions.cause: With the epoch heading attitude seeds (initial values only, not priors) the optimized body yaw slips one full turn against the GNSS-first course between minutes 3 and 13; without them the mount yaw stays at -176 deg.
submissions.rule: drop the seeds only where the optimized yaw slips a full turn (p95 deviation of body yaw minus course from its median above 90 deg); among the 40 test drives under the current recipe that is ebf-z alone (A505U slips without seeds and is open)
submissions.train_evidence_note: 14 checked train Pixel5 drives with seeds show no slip (p95 deviation at most 1.8 deg), so the rule changes no train drive; the evidence is truth-free
submissions.truth_free_diagnostic: horizontal distance to the archived taroz result_gnss_imu test output: median 0.19 -> 0.16 m, P95 1.01 -> 0.42 m; the seeded GCC control reproduces the submitted rows (P95 1.01 m)

submissions.cause: The IMU-stage yaw slipped one full turn between epochs 800 and 1400, a local minimum: with yaw = GNSS course + a constant 178.9 deg mount, the 1-s accelerometer matches the GNSS acceleration (along-track residual ~0, constant -0.5 m/s^2 cross-track), while dead-reckoned, velocity-heading and blended seeds all converge to the slipped basin.
submissions.rule: reseed only a drive whose yaw slips a full turn, with the mount estimated from the slip-free part of its first solution; keep the reseeded run only if the slip disappears and final-vs-GNSS-first P95 drops (A505U: 2.91 -> 1.38 m)
submissions.train_evidence_note: no train drive slips, so the rule changes no train score; course seeds on all five Samsung train drives leave four within 0.001 m and make mtv-n A205U worse (1.772 -> 5.675 m), which the final-vs-GNSS-first check flags (P95 2.32 -> 8.86 m)
submissions.truth_free_diagnostic: horizontal distance to the archived taroz result_gnss_imu test output: median 0.42 -> 0.34 m, P95 2.15 -> 0.88 m

taroz_comparison_notes.train_recipe_equivalent: 35 train drives with the per-phone test recipes: native mean (P50+P95)/2 0.718 m, taroz result_gnss_imu 0.712 m
taroz_comparison_notes.offset_convention: taroz result_gnss.mat and result_gnss_imu.mat already include add_position_offset (fgo_gnss.m / fgo_gnss_imu.m apply it before saving); compare them with the native final, not the native GNSS-first stage
taroz_comparison_notes.along_track: moving epochs: native along-track |error| median 0.314 m vs taroz 0.267 m, cross-track 0.295 vs 0.294 m; the excess is drive-specific (sm-a505g +0.79 vs +0.36 m), not a phone-family bias
taroz_comparison_notes.final_departs_from_gnss_first: train epochs where the native final is more than 0.8 m from the native GNSS-first (offset-aligned): the final is closer to truth in 82.7% of 7,985 epochs
taroz_comparison_notes.static_disagreement: train static epochs where native and taroz differ by more than 1 m: 102 epochs, taroz closer in 73%
taroz_comparison_notes.tdcp_arbiter: raw-ADR epoch-to-epoch displacement (robust LS, free clock) matches ground-truth steps to about 0.3 mm (10 ppm) at 29 m/s and stays within 0.00-0.12 m horizontally over 60-133 static epochs on train; compare it with trajectories converted exactly via ECEF/ENU (a spherical lat/lon conversion adds 0.19-0.24% scale error, which an earlier note mistook for TDCP drift); it cannot be used on phones whose ADR is unreliable (A325F, A32, S908B: 0.9-1.3 m per 30 s window)
taroz_comparison_notes.height_maps: test map drives vs relative-height drives: mean (P50+P95)/2 to taroz 0.375 vs 0.354 m; map points within 15 m spanning more than 2 m in height occur on at most 6% of epochs; removing the map moves mtv-b A325F 1.40 -> 1.38 m, sjc-r A32 0.81 -> 0.70 m and mtv-pe1 A325G 0.78 -> 0.84 m from taroz (not adopted)
taroz_comparison_notes.tdcp_scan_all_speeds: all 40 test drives, 30-s windows at all speeds: median disagreement 0.05-0.15 m for both pipelines where ADR is usable; native-only (> 0.5 m while taroz < 0.3 m) windows only on mtv-m Mi8 (1.06 m at a 7-satellite epoch, ambiguous) and mtv-a Mi8 (0.52 m); no second ebf-x-type failure
